facts.statement: The animal belongs to the genus Tarsistes.
The only known species is Tarsistes philippii.
The species was named by D. S. Jordan in 1919.
Tarsistes philippii is a member of the guitarfish family Rhinobatidae.
The species is known only from a single dried head found in the Juan Fernández Islands off Chile.
facts.quote: It is known only from a dried head from the Juan Fernández Islands off Chile.

facts.statement: The animal had a long, thin, flat snout that was rounded at the tip.
facts.quote: The head had a long, thin, flat snout, rounded at the tip like that of the goblin shark

facts.statement: The underside of the head was covered with small star-shaped prickles except at the base.
facts.quote: the underside covered with small stellate prickles except for the base

facts.statement: The head was covered with larger spinules, including six even larger ones that formed a curve around the eye.
facts.quote: The head was covered with larger spinules, with six still larger ones forming a curve around the eye

facts.statement: The original specimen was initially assigned to the genus Rhynchobatis by Philippi in 1858 without a specific species name.
facts.quote: The original specimen was assigned to the genus Rhynchobatis without a species name by Philippi in 1858

facts.statement: David Starr Jordan created the new name Tarsistes philippii in 1919 because the genus Rhynchobatis was already taken.
facts.quote: David Starr Jordan considered that genus name preoccupied (by Rhynchobatus) and coined the new scientific name Tarsistes philippii for it in 1919

facts.statement: Some researchers suggest that Tarsistes might be a synonym of the genus Pseudobatos.
facts.quote: In their revision of the generic alpha-taxonomy of Rhinobatidae, Last et al. (2016) considered Tarsistes a possible synonym of Pseudobatos

facts.statement: The animal is classified in the class Chondrichthyes.
No fossil occurrences for this genus have been recorded in the Paleobiology Database.

rejected.statement: The validity of the species is uncertain because the holotype has never been studied or described since its initial assignment.
rejected.quote: However, the holotype has never been studied or described since, so the status of this species is uncertain
